Items.Authors: Noemi Mezzanzanica, Ludovico Bizzarri, Giulia Rancati Cattaneo, Andrea Limonta, Mario Zannoni, Giuseppe Addamo, Mauro Lumia, Oscar A. Peverini
Items.Title: Additive manufacturing ultralight profiled feed horns for space-based sky observations
Items.Abstract: Profiled horn antennas for spaceborne astronomical observations have been prototyped in the 80-170 GHz band using Laser Powder Bed Fusion on Metal (LPBF/M) technology, enabling the fabrication of lightweight, monolithic metallic structures with highly controlled geometries. The LPBF/M process allows the realization of optimized horn profiles capable of delivering low return loss, high beam symmetry, and stable broadband performance essential for cosmic microwave background and sub-millimeter astrophysics missions. The flexibility of additive manufacturing also supports rapid design iteration and scalable array production, making LPBF/M a promising pathway for next-generation high-frequency focal-plane architectures in space astronomy. Towards the assessment of a high TRL, mechanical tests and cryogenic thermal cycling are foreseen.

Items.Authors: Claire Tonsa, Enrico Virgilli, Adriano De Rosa, Carmelo Gargano, Natalia Auricchio, Giovanni De Cesare, Claudio Ferrari, Elena Ferrari, Giuseppe Baldazzi, Riccardo Campana, Ezio Caroli, Marta Civitani, Raffaella Landi, Giuseppe Levi, John B. Stephen, John Rankin, Alfonso Pisapia
Items.Title: Adjustable gamma-ray optics (AGO): active alignment for high-precision Laue lenses
Items.Abstract: Hard X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy above ~70 keV needs focusing optics beyond current capabilities. Laue lenses are the most promising solution, but their development is limited by the challenge of aligning thousands of crystals with arcsecond precision. Adhesive-based mountings introduce angular deviations that exceed requirements. We present “Adjustable Gamma-ray Optics” (AGO), a concept enabling arcsecond alignment and active tuning of each Laue-lens crystal via monolithic flexures actuated by miniature piezo stacks. Each Si(111) crystal is mounted on a tunable lamella, allowing sub-arcsecond Bragg-angle control with minimal area loss. This architecture improves alignment, reduces thermal and mechanical sensitivity, and enables in-flight tuning. A 9-crystal demonstrator with bent crystals, optimized flexures, low-absorption routing, and first alignment strategies validates the approach, paving the way for tunable, high-precision lenses for future missions.

Items.Authors: Wim Pessemier, Gert Raskin, Jacob Pember, Jesus Pérez Padilla, Pieter Vuylsteke, Wim De Meester, Maddalena Reggiani, Christian Schwab, Bart Vandenbussche, Hans Van Winckel
Items.Title: Advanced PLC-based control at the heart of the MARVEL telescope array
Items.Abstract: MARVEL is a high-resolution spectrograph fed by four telescopes, currently being commissioned at the Mercator Observatory on La Palma. At the core of the facility's control architecture is a powerful TwinCAT PLC, which not only manages local devices but also coordinates large parts of the entire facility. We highlight the use of industrial vision for fast tip-tilt guiding, the integration of ASCOM/Alpaca devices, and the implementation of a flexible task sequencer for instrument configuration, all on the PLC platform. The system makes extensive use of a web-based TwinCAT HMI for visualizing these features and for rendering basic 3D views of parts of the facility. Additionally, we describe how an improved model-driven code generation framework has enabled us to efficiently deploy fundamental code changes across the system, to migrate decade-old Mercator code to the most recent PLC platforms, and to drastically reduce HMI CPU load by introducing a Model-View-Controller architecture.

Items.Authors: Matteo Canzari, Fiore De Luise, Mauro Dolci, Gaetano Valentini, Andrea Baldassarre, Simone Benedetti, Filippo Boschi, Amico Di Cianno, Nicola Napoleone, Massimo Quintini, Angelo Valentini
Items.Title: Advancing operations at the Campo Imperatore observing station: integrated modernization of telescopes and infrastructure
Items.Abstract: The Campo Imperatore observing station on the Gran Sasso plateau hosts Italy’s highest professional VIS/NIR facility. Two 1-m telescopes, VIT and WOT, are undergoing a coordinated modernization of hardware, control systems, and software infrastructure. VIT is being upgraded with the new CI2RCE InGaAs NIR imager and enhanced control capabilities, while WOT receives updated electronics. Additional developments include site-wide environmental monitoring, extended control hardware, and an integrated software layer for unified operations. This work presents the current configuration of the station and the ongoing refurbishment efforts, aimed at improving reliability, availability, and full remote operability, and outlines the planned return of VIT to scientific operations with its upgraded instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Jorge D. Llop-Sayson, Chaoyin Zhou, Anita M. Fisher, Garreth J. Ruane, Eugene Serabyn, Dimitri P. Mawet
Items.Title: Advancing vector vortex coronagraph technology for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The vortex coronagraph offers an efficient solution to starlight suppression: it provides high starlight suppression while maintaining excellent throughput for off-axis sources. The leading approach to fabricate a vortex coronagraph mask relies on liquid crystal polymers (LCPs), producing what is known as the vector vortex coronagraph (VVC). The main limitation of the VVC arises from mask fabrication errors, which result in a contrast floor above the requirements of HWO. Here, we report recent progress at JPL’s Microdevices Laboratory (MDL) toward fabricating VVC masks for HWO.

Items.Authors: Thomas Essinger-Hileman, Alyssa Barlis, Charles Bennett, Yan Yan (Carol) Chan, Michael Chauby, Haiquan Guo, Kyle Helson, Adriana Macris, Sadeq Malakooti, Manuel Quijada, Maryam Rahmani, Evan Steinberg, Stephanie Vivod, Edward Wollack
Items.Title: Aerogels to reduce optical reflections
Items.Abstract: We present initial demonstrations of electromagnetic absorbers to reduce optical reflections fabricated by incorporating carbon particles into polymer aerogel materials. Instruments in the microwave through far-IR are strongly affected by thermal emission from even rather cold surfaces, so careful control of stray light is required to avoid reduced instrument sensitivity. Polymer aerogels offer a unique material system featuring low mass density and index of refraction in addition to tunable optical properties through inclusion of particles. We present the design, fabrication, and characterization of stray-light reduction sheets and molded calibrator targets based on carbon-loaded aerogel material. This technology offers significant improvement in performance (reduced reflectance) as well as lower size and weight compared with current state of the art for stray light reduction or calibrator targets.

Items.Authors: Christophe S. Clergeon
Items.Title: ALTAIR Gemini North SCAO: challenges & performances review
Items.Abstract: ALTAIR, the facility Single-Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) system for the Gemini North Telescope, has been providing on-sky performance for over twenty years. While Gemini Observatory advances next-generation AO capabilities, High-Strehl ExAO, wide-field LTAO and MOAO concepts, and GLAO facilities, ALTAIR remains a critical asset. Despite the challenges associated with operating and maintaining an aging, first-generation SCAO instrument, it continues to support frontline science on Gemini North. In this contribution, we will present the current status of ALTAIR, outline the operational and technical challenges faced in the context of a maturing AO facility, and describe the ongoing strategy to sustain and enhance SCAO performance at Gemini North during this important transition periode

Items.Authors: David D. S. Hale, Prakriti Gupta
Items.Title: An improved waveform definition language
Items.Abstract: We present an updated Waveform Definition Language (WDL), a high-level, modular language for defining and compiling detector readout waveforms for CCD, CMOS and hybrid detector systems. Developed for the STA Archon controller and its Archon Configuration File (ACF) format, WDL 2.0 provides a more intuitive, structured syntax that simplifies the creation and maintenance of complex timing patterns. The waveform compiler, significantly improved since our first implementation in 2017, translates symbolic timing rules and parameterized definitions into controller-ready configuration files. Improved error diagnostics and visualization tools enable immediate feedback and waveform timing validation prior to deployment, reducing development and debugging effort.

Items.Authors: Dominic F. Sanchez, Philip Hinz, Renate Kupke, Deno Stelter, Daren Dillon, Cari Johnston
Items.Title: An infrared spectropolarimeter for measuring the 3-micron water-ice feature in protoplanetary disks
Items.Abstract: We present the design of a reflective dispersive Wollaston prism spectropolarimetric mode for the SCALES instrument, enabling simultaneous infrared spectropolarimetry of protoplanetary disks across the 2–4 micron band. The mode provides measurement of orthogonal linear polarization states in a compact configuration compatible with SCALES’ reflective architecture and prism wheel infrastructure. Optical modeling confirms that the reflective double-pass geometry provides sufficient beam separation and spectral coverage across the 3-micron water-ice band, with resolution adequate to resolve the feature. Spectropolarimetric simulations using synthetic data demonstrate sensitivity to scattering-induced polarization, enabling constraints on snow-line location, grain growth, and dust composition.    This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. This document number is LLNL-ABS-2013969.

Items.Authors: Dorian Paillon, Michelle Galloway, Sean Sellers, Lucia Kleint
Items.Title: An interactive Python simulation for echelle spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Echelle spectrographs are used worldwide for ground-based astronomy, both nighttime and daytime. Such  instruments increase the complexity of an optical design and add additional parameters to optimize for one’s  science case. We developed an interactive Python simulation dedicated to simplify their early design phase called  SIESTA (Simulating Interactive Echelle Spectroscopy for Targeted Applications). The available features include  an interactive display of the selected spectral range as well as the possibility to show detailed spectral information  (e.g. spectral resolution) for every simulated points of any specified number of slits. This program idea, probing the use of Integral-Field Units with Echelle spectrographs, stems from the complex design of the Solar and stellar Wide-Spectral coverage Polarimeter (SoWiSP), notably putting stringent constraints on the imaging camera system. We have used SIESTA to guide the design of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Briley L. Lewis, Manxuan Zhang, Maxwell A. Millar-Blanchaer, Jayke Nguyen, Ashish Uhlmann, Max Brodheim
Items.Title: An open-source data processing pipeline for Keck / NIRC2 polarimetry
Items.Abstract: The Keck/NIRC2 infrared imager was recently upgraded with a new suite of polarimetric observing modes. This polarimetry upgrade (referred to as NIRC2-Pol) will open up a wide range of new astronomical studies, including investigations of exoplanets, the Galactic center, active galactic nuclei and the solar system. Astronomical polarimeters require sophisticated data reduction, especially for quantitative polarimetry requiring the use of a Mueller Matrix model for instrumental polarization calibration. This work presents a flexible, user-friendly data processing pipeline intended for use with NIRC2-Pol, summarizing its key steps and implementation details. The software is open-source, and written such that it should be straightforwardly adaptable to other dual-channel polarimeters in astronomy, such as Subaru/SCExAO/CHARIS.

Items.Authors: Renbin Yan, Yutong Qiao, Ruoyu Zhou, Qingjiu Chen, Chit-Ho Hui, Sabyasachi Chattopadhyay, Yuguang Chen, Zhuo Cheng, Yee-Ching Lam, Zhiheng Lin, Ziming Peng, Michael P. Smith, Guangquan Zeng, Jichen Zhang
Items.Title: An updated and complete design of the jockey club spectroscopy survey system
Items.Abstract: The Jockey Club Spectroscopy Survey System (JCS3) is the northern hemisphere prototype for the Affordable Multiple Aperture Spectroscopy Explorer (AMASE). This paper presents a comprehensive redesign of the entire system. The updated spectrograph employs a Maksutov-style collimator with a meniscus corrector and a custom objective lens, paired with a larger CMOS detector. This optical overhaul drastically reduces vignetting and improves image quality, enabling higher spectral resolution. A novel double-sided slit fiber system allows two primary science telescopes (0.14m & 0.8m apertures) to share a single spectrograph. Each telescope feeds a dedicated 1519-fiber hexagonal bundle, with the 0.8m telescope using a microlens array to couple with fibers. Three supporting telescopes provide continuous sky monitoring and flux calibration via fibers interlaced with science targets on the slit. We also detail the focal plane module, calibration unit, and protective enclosure.

Items.Authors: Veronica Baldini, Igor Coretti, Paolo Cucurullo, Antonio Sulich, Anna Brucalassi, Giorgio Calderone, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alen Khanbekyan, Alessandro Marconi, Matteo Porru, Enrico Pinna, Monica Rainer, Marcello Scalera, Chiara Selmi, Andrea Tozzi, Alessio Zanutta, P. Berio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: control electronics and software for the adaptive optics and integral field units
Items.Abstract: The ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) is a second-generation instrument for ESO’s ELT, designed to deliver ultra-stable, high-resolution spectroscopy from the visible to the near-infrared. It will enable breakthrough science, from detecting Earth-like exoplanets to measuring cosmic acceleration. ANDES relies on two key subsystems: the SCAO module, which provides diffraction-limited correction of atmospheric turbulence, and the IFU, which reformats and injects the corrected beam into the spectrograph fiber with high efficiency. This work presents the design of the control electronics and software for both subsystems. The architecture is based on Beckhoff programmable logic controllers (PLCs) integrated within the ELT Instrument Control Framework (IFW), ensuring compliance with ESO standards for communication, synchronization, and safety.

Items.Authors: Giorgio Calderone, Elena Mason, Matteo Porru, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Marco Landoni, Manuel Monteiro
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: the star avoidance algorithm
Items.Abstract: ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) is the high-resolution, fiber fed spectrograph foreseen  to be installed as a second-generation instrument on the upcoming ELT (Extremely Large Telescope). Equipped  with two movable arms, ANDES is able to simultaneously collect light from the science target and the sky  background, with a sky-projected distance between the fibers 15”≥ d ≥132”. Since there is no field derotator,  the sky background fiber will sample different patches of the sky during an exposure. In this paper we describe  the “ANDES star avoidance” algorithm to automatically calculate the initial position, and the shifts to be applied  on the sky arm during an exposure, to keep it at a safe distance from all possible astrophysical sources and avoid  light contamination.

Items.Authors: S. D'Auria, A. Tozzi, A. Brucalassi, A. Khanbekyan, P. Picchi, M. Rainer, M. Aliverti, E. Redaelli, A. Zanutta, F. D'Anca, E. Oliva
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: IFU mechanical design and FE analysis
Items.Abstract: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ESO ELT, is advancing toward system-level PDR, following the successful Preliminary design review (PDR) of its Integral Field Unit (IFU). This paper reports the setup of the mechanical model used for Finite Element Analysis (FEA) of the IFU. Starting from the optical design, an initial mechanical layout was produced to evaluate the preliminary opto-mechanical interfaces and structural constraints. The IFU has been decomposed into its main mechanical assemblies and optical mounts to quantify volume, mass, interface loads, and alignment-critical regions. The analysis assesses global and local stiffness, thermal deformation, dynamic response, and seismic resilience, providing input for material selection, mounting strategies, and stability budgeting in preparation for detailed design.

Items.Authors: Tom Seccull, Ioannis Apergis, Leonidas Asimakoulas, Colin G. Coates, Darren Frew, Jouni Jussila
Items.Title: Andor Toran: a versatile sCMOS camera platform for astronomy and physical science
Items.Abstract: We present the new Andor Toran, a compact, robust, and versatile camera platform designed to support a range of sCMOS sensors. The first Toran camera to launch is the Toran-PS 26B which integrates the 26 megapixel IMX571 sensor from Sony. This large format, high resolution, back-illuminated sensor offers high sensitivity, native 16-bit digitization, and full-frame readout in under 150 ms. With these specifications, exceptionally low dark current, and practically zero amplifier glow, Toran’s first sensor ensures that sensitive, reliable, and quantitatively robust wide-field astronomical survey imaging is supported across a broad range of survey cadences and exposure times with small optically fast survey telescopes. Alongside the properties of the Toran-PS 26B that support its practicality and performance in astronomical imaging, we will outline the roadmap for future development of Toran as a camera platform.

Items.Authors: Ichiro Jikuya, Yoichi Tamura, Akio Taniguchi, Masaki Sakakibara, Akinobu Miyake, Masato Hagimoto, Kianhong Lee, Chihiro Imamura, Shion Takeno, Sachiko Okumura, Nozomi Okada
Items.Title: Anti-windup PI controller for millimeter-wave adaptive optics: a Nobeyama 45m radio telescope simulation
Items.Abstract: This work addresses the control problem for Millimeter-wave Adaptive Optics (MAO), which we define as compensating for the optical path length variation between the primary reflector (M1) and the receiver at the focal point. We utilize a measurement system developed by Tamura et al. to track these variations.  The challenge is formalized as an asymptotic constant disturbance rejection problem. We demonstrate that the closed-loop control by an anti-windup proportional-integral (AWPI) controller effectively solves this problem while respecting the physical movement constraints of the optical driving system. Simulation results, based on the Nobeyama 45-m Telescope with a two-axis translating sub-reflector (M2), validate the performance of the proposed AWPI approach. This  approach establishes a foundation for metrology in future large-aperture submillimeter facilities such as AtLAST/LST.

Items.Authors: Dan Sirbu, Rachel Morgan, Ruslan Belikov, Eduardo Bendek, Kevin Fogarty, Jonathan Lin, Kevin Sims, Carson Valdez, Anne Kroo, Olav Solgaard, David A. B. Miller
Items.Title: AstroPIC III: advancing the near-infrared photonic integrated coronagraph for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), identified as the top priority flagship for astrophysics in the 2020 Decadal Survey, requires a coronagraph instrument reaching ten orders of magnitude starlight suppression to directly image Earth-like planets. Coronagraphs based on Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) offer potentially game-changing advantages for this mission by combining the efficiency and aggressive inner working angles of advanced nulling architectures with the compactness and reconfigurability of integrated photonics.    This third paper in the series provides an overview of technology development efforts for AstroPIC, a near-infrared photonic integrated coronagraph concept for HWO. We review the design and recent high contrast results for AstroPIC, which reached better than 1e-9 contrast ratios with our silicon PIC prototype, including functional system-level demonstrations with a free-space coupling system. We outline the near-infrared science enabled including compati

Items.Authors: Randolph Hammond, John C. Wilson, Stephen A. Smee, Robert H. Barkhouser, Nancy J. Chanover, William Ketzeback, Aidan Gray, Josh Peebles, Stephen Hope
Items.Title: Atmospheric dispersion corrector for the ARC 3.5m telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the design for an Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC) to be deployed on Nasmyth port 1 (NA1) of the Astrophysical Research Consortium (ARC) 3.5-m Telescope at Apache Point Observatory in New Mexico. The ADC, placed within the NA1 altitude bearing bore, will serve the existing Echelle spectrograph (ARCES) as well as its proposed successor (ASPEN) and require no permanent modifications to the telescope structure. The ADC consists of two, 90mm diameter, counter-rotating prism assemblies. The prisms are mounted within the rotors of servo ring motors, each supported on single 4-point contact thin section ball bearings. Absolute position feedback for the servo motors is provided by magnetic encoders. We will share a detailed system diagram as well as proposed control software architecture designed to interface with telescope operation.

Items.Authors: Sanele Hlabisa, Sydil Kupa, Alex Smith
Items.Title: AutoScheduler: a full-stack AI framework for optimizing MeerKAT telescope utilization
Items.Abstract: Scheduling observations for the MeerKAT Radio Telescope is currently a manual, labor-intensive process prone to inefficiencies. This work introduces AutoScheduler, a full-stack framework that automates scheduling by addressing complex astronomical constraints, including Earth’s rotation, horizon visibility, and solar proximity. We explored three optimization techniques: a Genetic Algorithm, Monte Carlo Tree Search, and a Greedy Search Heuristic. Our results demonstrate that these AI-driven approaches can reproduce three-month schedules with a 30× speedup over manual methods, successfully scheduling 60% of observations without conflicts. The system includes a web-based application to visualize generated timetables and monitor Local Sidereal Time window utilization, allowing operators to easily identify gaps. This framework provides a scalable foundation for maximizing telescope science output through automated, intelligent planning.

Items.Authors: Alan Hsu, Jenna Samra, Steven Tomczyk, Daniel Durusky, Jacob Hawthorne, Vanessa Marquez, Abigail Unger
Items.Title: Calibrating the CORSAIR polarimeter for its qualification flight
Items.Abstract: We show preliminary results for a probabilistic calibration of the CORSAIR polarimeter that quantifies the calibration uncertainty explicitly. First, we place a calibration unit in front of the polarimeter to generate known Stokes inputs. Using an infrared source and detector, we project light through the system and record the observed intensities at different modulation states. We model our polarimeter using a probabilistic Mueller matrix framework and estimate the posterior distribution of the free parameters, effectively computing the calibration uncertainty in the form of a distribution shift on our initial estimates. We find that the CORSAIR polarimeter waveplate is consistent with the expected quarter-waveplate behavior, and that the inferred downstream Stokes efficiencies satisfy the system requirements. We also find that field-angle variations in the calibrated parameters across the optic are smaller than the recovered posterior uncertainties.

Items.Authors: Cuán de Barra, Padraig McDermott, Derek O'Callaghan, Alexey Uliyanov, David Murphy, Sheila McBreen
Items.Title: Calibration and characterization campaign of the GIFTS 8U CubeSat gamma-ray detector payload
Items.Abstract: Gamma-Ray Investigation of the Full Transient Sky (GIFTS) is an 8U CubeSat designed to observe and localize GRBs from low-Earth orbit in the Multi-messenger era. Presented here are the results of the extensive characterization campaign for the gamma-ray detector payload performed in UCD which complement and verify Monte Carlo simulations of the detector performance required for GRB localization. Results include the spectral resolution, effective area, and angular response of the GIFTS detectors, as well as calibration functions to convert from detector to energy space. Finally, the results of ground-based testing of GIFTS’ triggering and localization ability are shown, highlighting the mission’s capabilities and importance to the gamma-ray fleet.

Items.Authors: Sarah Steiger, Rémi Soummer, Raphaël Pourcelot, Emiel H. Por, Laurent Pueyo, Iva Laginja, Nathan Scott
Items.Title: Calibration of MEMS DM actuator gains using a Zernike wavefront sensor on the HiCAT testbed and implications for Habitable Worlds Observatory operations
Items.Abstract: Deformable mirrors (DMs) are critical for coronagraph operations on ground-based telescopes and future missions like HWO and Roman CGI. They enable wavefront control to create a high-contrast “dark zone” (DZ) for detecting faint companions. Achieving contrasts <1e-8 requires precise DM actuator-gain calibration, as picometer-level errors degrade DZ digging efficiency, increase overheads, and tighten stability requirements. Because DM gain varies with stroke, rapid in situ recalibration is needed. Zernike wavefront sensors (ZWFS) offer picometer sensitivity and will likely be onboard HWO, but their use for DM calibration remains unproven and has major operational implications. We present HiCAT testbed results calibrating gain maps for two 952-actuator BMC MEMS DMs with both a Fizeau interferometer and a ZWFS. We show that the ZWFS achieves sub-nm sensitivity and supports gain maps using local linear or quadratic models with implications for final DZ contrast and digging efficiency.

Items.Authors: Ida Sigusch, Antonin Besse, Pierre Piron, Imran Khan, Aurèle Adam, Jérôme Loicq
Items.Title: CAPIBARA: An experimental multiwavelength beam combination testbench for space-based nulling interferometry
Items.Abstract: The rising interest of the astronomical community in observing and characterizing earth-like exoplanets led to rising interest in a space-based, mid-infrared (2-20μm) nulling interferometric mission concept. Following the legacy of ground-based stellar interferometers, testbenches dedicated to different aspects of nulling interferometry are under development.  The Space Instrumentation Group at TU Delft is developing a testbench focusing on aspects concerning the multiwavelength and four beam combination in nulling interferometry. The focus of the experiments will be on different beam combination strategies as well as the effects and applications of polarization in a nulling interferometer.   In this communication, we will report on the design and performance of our multiwavelength (4 μm, 8 μm, 12 μm) four beam testbench. Special focus will be on the spectral coalignment and generation of the four coherent beams which are feeding our experiments.

Items.Authors: Abhradeep Roy, Yusuke Suda, Yasushi Fukazawa, Norito Nakano, Koume Sakano, Regina Caputo, Daniel P. Violette, Adrien Laviron, Carolyn A. Kierans, Grant Sommer, Jeremy S. Perkins, John W. Mitchell, Lucia Tian, Ryan C. Boggs, Manoj Jadhav, Bobae Kim, Jessica E. Metcalfe, Nicolas Striebig, Richard Leys, Ivan Peric, Hiroyasu Tajima, Shin Kushima, Simon Spannagel, Lennart Huth, Elizaveta Sitnikova, Luca Baldini, Anna Driutti
Items.Title: Characterization and simulation of AstroPix for future space missions
Items.Abstract: Next-generation medium-energy (100 keV–100 MeV) gamma-ray missions require low-power, high-resolution, and highly scalable pixelated detectors. AstroPix, a monolithic HV-CMOS active pixel sensor being developed for the proposed AMEGO-X telescope, aims to meet these needs with ~1.5 mW/cm² power consumption, ~500 µm spatial resolution, 10% energy resolution at 122 keV, and fully depleted silicon layer. A 2×2 AstroPix array, the “quad-chip”, forms a 4×4 cm² module and the basic unit of AMEGO-X’s large-area tracker. We report characterization of the AstroPix v3 quad-chips and introduce A-STEP, a three-layer sounding-rocket payload designed to validate AstroPix in space. We utilized the Geant4-based MEGAlib simulation package to predict event rates, spectra of deposited energy, and reconstruction of the direction of incident particles during the A-STEP flight.

Items.Authors: Claire Tonsa, Enrico Virgilli, Nicolas Barriere, Casper van Aarle, Max Collon, Piero Rosati
Items.Title: Characterization of a silicon-based Laue-lens element for future soft-gamma-ray modular focusing optics
Items.Abstract: A SiLC (Silicon Laue Component) demonstrator manufactured by cosine (The Netherlands) has been tested at the LARIX facility of the University of Ferrara, Italy. The SiLC focuses X-rays through Bragg diffraction in transmission (Laue) geometry using thin bent silicon plates. Its performance was evaluated with a collimated X-ray beam traveling 26.5 m before reaching the crystal, reproducing astrophysical conditions.  The spatial and energy distributions of the diffracted photons allow us to assess the SiLC focusing capabilities—examining diffraction uniformity along the sagittal curvature and plate alignment—its energy bandpass through meridional curvature, and its peak reflectivity and diffraction efficiency. Experimental results and their comparison with Monte Carlo simulations reproducing the test conditions will be presented.

Items.Authors: Elijah Kane, Peter S. Barry, Chris Benson, Charles (Matt) Bradford, Thomas Brien, Simon Doyle, Victor Gómez-Rivera, Steve Hailey-Dunsheath, Jesús Hernández-Aguilar, José Luis Hérnandez-Rebollar, David H. Hughes, Kirit Karkare, Alex Lapuente, Ryan McGeehan, Raúl Naranjo-Romero, Andreas Papageorgiou, Joseph Redford, Iván Rodríguez Montoya, Sam Rowe, David Sánchez-Arguelles, Sofia Savorgnano, Annie Tan, Marcial Tapia, Jair Vega-Méndez
Items.Title: Characterization of filterbank performance for the SuMAC submillimeter spectrometer
Items.Abstract: The SuperSpec-MUSCAT collaboration (SuMAC) is the joint effort to operate the SuperSpec spectrometer in the MUSCAT cryostat at the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT). SuperSpec is an on-chip spectrometer developed to greatly reduce the size and thermal mass of a submillimeter spectrometer. SuperSpec uses lithographically patterned filters which couple to kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) on a silicon chip with an area of only a few square centimeters. The first light of SuMAC took place at the LMT in Summer 2025, with successful observations of submillimeter-bright sources and LIM-style scans. Three polarization-sensitive pixels were deployed, two of which each cover the 190 – 300 GHz atmospheric window, with a moderate spectral resolution of R~200. In this poster, I present the spectral characterization of the filterbanks of the SuMAC instrument, using Fourier-transform and swept-source measurements, as well as full filter bank modeling.

Items.Authors: Kian Syaifoel, Himadri Saha, Felix Münning, Matthias Justen, Netty Honingh, Jochem Baselmans, Dominik Riechers
Items.Title: Characterization of materials and fabrication methods for an MKID filterbank spectrometer for line- intensity mapping of [CII]
Items.Abstract: We are developing an on-chip filterbank spectrometer with the aim of performing line-intensity mapping of [CII] with the CCAT/FYST telescope. We target the 220 GHz - 440 GHz band, with a spectral resolution of R ~ 100. We present the kinetic inductance measurements of our sputtered Al films, which are needed for the design of our MKIDs. We also present our progress in fabrication methods, including a double-resist liftoff method in which we locally control the resist thickness and undercut. We furthermore look into the surface and interface treatments of our samples, in particular with respect to the quality of the NbTiN-Al interface and the sources of TLS noise.

Items.Authors: Simone Pagliarella, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Paolo Soffitta, Enrico Costa, Alessandro Di Marco, Alessandro Lacerenza, Fabio Muleri, Stefano Silvestri, Nicolas De Angelis
Items.Title: Characterization of solar background signatures in IXPE gas pixel detectors through laboratory measurements
Items.Abstract: We present a laboratory–to–flight comparison of the IXPE background signatures, using the spare Detector Unit (DU), identical to the three flight units, exposed to a Co-60 radioactive source, historically adopted as a proxy for solar-induced X-ray background. Co-60 emits 1.17 MeV photons which undergo Compton scattering in the DU structures, producing a degraded spectrum peaking at ~2 keV after ADC counts→keV conversion via Fe-55 (charging measurement) calibration. The source was placed on the top and side of the DU; event tracks were reconstructed to extract spectral and morphological observables (size track, energy fraction in the track’s main cluster, number of pixel hit per event). Lab spectra and parameter distributions are compared with IXPE in-flight in-eclipse (Earth occultating the sun) and in-sun backgrounds from observations. We discuss how the in-flight and on-ground spectral and modulation properties of the background compare to each other.

Items.Authors: Anna K. Gagnebin, Kevin Bundy, Aditya R. Sengupta, Matthew DeMartino, Daren Dillon, Tara Crowe, Caleb Dobias, Stephen S. Eikenberry, Rodrigo Amezcua Correa, Stephanos Yerolatsitis, Holger Schmidt, Avi Patel, Andrew Bradshaw
Items.Title: Characterizing spectral reconstruction performance of a photonic lantern
Items.Abstract: The photonic lantern (PL) is an optical waveguide commonly made by tapering a bundle of single-mode fibers into a multi-mode facet. PLs have been used for coupling multimode light to photonic devices, and more recently for wavefront sensing. By allowing only a single-mode input from a broadband source, the PL – paired with a machine learning spectral reconstruction algorithm – can also be used as a low-resolution spectrometer. Here, we present spectral reconstruction results as a function of the input wavelength in NIR to assess how deviations from a PL design wavelength of 1550 nm affect performance. This work demonstrates a path towards dynamically modulating PL spectrometer systems in order to achieve customized performance in terms of spectral resolution and bandwidth.

Items.Authors: Mingyi Ding, Jing Chen, Liang Wang, Kai Zhang, Jean Louis Lizon, Qiqige Xin, Dinghao Feng
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: design and optimization of the exposure meter towards extreme precise radial velocity
Items.Abstract: The CHORUS is a state-of-the-art instrument developed for the 10.4 m GTC telescope in Spain. One of the scientific motivations is to perform the precise radial velocity (PRV) measurement of sub-m/s, to detect habitable rocky planets around solar-type stars, which in turns require an accurate photon-weighted mean time of exposure (MTE) to conduct the barycentric Earth radial velocity (BERV) correction. We simulated the requirements on resolution and frame rate of a chromatic expsure-meter (EXM) operating synchronously with the visiable-band spectrograph (VIS) of CHORUS. Our simulation accounts for the total instrument throughput and variations in atmoshperic conditions, including changes in airmass and thin cloud transient. Finally, we present the optical design of EXM on CHORUS with the optimized configuration, and demonstrated that the MTE calculated with the proposed strategy can fulfill the precision requirement for BERV correction, thereby supporting the PRV science using CHORUS.

Items.Authors: Elana K. Urbach, Brian Brondel, Franco Colleoni, Felipe Daruich, Erik Dennihy, Johnny Esteves, Ellie Hileman, Petr Kubánek, Fritz Mueller, Freddy Muñoz Arancibia, Douglas R. Neill, Jérémy Neveu, Kevin Reil, Mario F. Rivera, Malhar Sonaniskar, Brian Stalder, Sandrine Thomas, Roberto Tighe, Yousuke Utsumi
Items.Title: Commissioning and performance of the M1M3 thermal control system for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
Items.Abstract: The M1M3 mirror for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory is a cast borosilicate monolith. With its relatively high thermal coefficient of expansion and large variation in thickness across the monolith, the thermal control system is critical. We discuss the commissioning and early performance of the M1M3 thermal system, which involves temperature controlled air entering each honeycomb cell of the mirror through an air nozzle, before returning and being reconditioned by fan coil units. We discuss how we use this system to cool the mirror to one degree below ambient. We also present an analysis of thermal gradients in the glass measured with 146 thermocouples in the glass, and show progress in mitigating the gradients as we work to reduce both thermal distortion and mirror seeing.

Items.Authors: Arturo Osorio, Benjamín González, Esteban Vera
Items.Title: Compact AO system for Cassegrain Telescopes: design and implementation for a 50cm aperture
Items.Abstract: We present the optical design and implementation of a compact adaptive optics system to be mounted on small Cassegrain telescopes, particularly a 50cm telescope used at the SEETRUE Optical Grund Station located in Valparaiso, Chile. This compact design allows us to operate a robotic mount without a significant weight increment along with our 50cm Ritchey Chretien telescope. By using an off-the-shelf piezo electric deformable mirror and a custom non-modulated pyramid wavefront sensor, our system enables real-time tip/tilt correction as well as aberrations up to the first 37 Zernike modes when closing the adaptive optics loop while observing stars affected atmospheric turbulence. In this work we describe the optical design, passive and active optical elements, hardware and software used for real time control. At the moment the system is being implemented and has been tested on the optical bench with an emulated telescope.

Items.Authors: Makoto Yoshihara, Yusuke Yoshida, Yamato Ishida, Kazuki Ampuku, Koki Sakuta, Keitoku Yoshihira, Tetuo Kano, Naoki Ishida, Yoichi Yatsu, Yoshizumi Miyoshi, Kazushi Asamura, Noriko Yamasaki, Toru Tamagawa, Noriyuki Narukage, Yoshitaka Inoue, Takashi Okajima, Keisuke Tamura, Kikuko Miyata, Gota Yamaguchi, Shutaro Mohri, Takehiro Kume, Yusuke Matsuzawa, Yoichi Imamura, Takahiro Saito, Kentaro Hiraguri, Hirokazu Hashizume, Hidekazu Mimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi
Items.Title: Compact, high-sensitivity x-ray imaging spectroscopic instruments for CubeSats: development status
Items.Abstract: We have been developing a compact high-sensitivity X-ray imaging spectroscopic instrument for CubeSats. We have two optics designs: 100mm and 250mm in focal length, for 6U and 500mm-class CubeSats. Currently, we have completed the conceptual designs of our instruments, and a prototype was actually fabricated.   For the prototype instrument with two sample mirrors (φ20 and 40mm), we conducted the vibration tests in the z-axis direction for the first time. We applied the vibration level required for a sounding rocket. Consequently, no significant changes were observed through visual inspection. Furthermore, to quantitatively evaluate the load on the mirrors, we focused on the vibration response of the mirrors and confirmed resonance frequencies at 330 and 500 Hz corresponding to bending modes. These modes contribute more than two-thirds of the total load. In this presentation, the status of scientific feasibility study and instrument development will be reported.

Items.Authors: Yamato Ishida, Yusuke Yoshida, Makoto Yoshihara, Koki Sakuta, Kazuki Ampuku, Keitoku Yoshihira, Tetsuo Kano, Naoki Ishida, Yoichi Yatsu, Yoshizumi Miyoshi, Kazushi Asamura, Noriko Yamasaki, Toru Tamagawa, Noriyuki Narukage, Yoshitaka Inoue, Takashi Okajima, Keisuke Tamura, Kikuko Miyata, Gota Yamaguchi, Shutaro Mohri, Takehiro Kume, Yusuke Matsuzawa, Yoichi Imamura, Takahiro Saito, Kentaro Hiraguri, Hirokazu Hashizume, Hidekazu Mimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi
Items.Title: Compact, high-sensitivity x-ray imaging spectroscopic instruments for CubeSats: simulations
Items.Abstract: We are developing a compact high-sensitivity X-ray imaging spectroscopic instrument for small spacecraft such as CubeSats. Assuming a 6U CubeSat (100×200×300 mm), we conducted simulations based on a nested Wolter type-I mirror design with a focal length of 100 mm, total length of 100 mm, and apertures of 5, 10, and 20 mm. As a result, the imaging performance degraded more rapidly than in long-focal-length systems even when only geometric aberrations were considered, reaching HPD~50″ at an off-axis angle of 10′ at 1 keV. The HPD value also depended on an aperture size: at a 10′ off-axis angle, 5 mm and 20 mm single mirrors exhibited HPDs of ~300″ and ~30″, respectively. In addition, a stray light component specific to nested structures, such as backside reflections, appeared beyond 30′ off-axis. This poster presents these results for the 100-mm focal-length system and also results for 500×500×500 mm-class CubeSats.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Meoli, Olaf Iwert, Omar Sqalli, Elizabeth George, Mathias Richerzhagen, Alexander Rüde, Matthias Seidel, Samuel Lévêque
Items.Title: Conceptual architecture of the detector infrastructure for WST
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) is a proposed 12 m wide-field spectroscopic facility combining several multi-object spectrographs. It requires a yet unprecedented number of detectors. In this paper we present a conceptual architecture for the detector controller and infrastructure required to operate a large number of detectors, potentially applicable to WST, focusing on the system-level, power distribution, and the associated data handling. We also consider how these elements may evolve over the expected development timeline of such a facility.  Motivated by the scale of the problem, we outline a possible distributed detector-controller architecture, based on modular units placed close to the detectors and networked backend electronics.

Items.Authors: Matteo Menessini, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Marco Xompero, Christian Patanauer, Ciro del Vecchio
Items.Title: Contactless deformable mirror for space telescopes: operations and electro-mechanical characterization
Items.Abstract: Contactless DM systems are widely the state-of-the art for adaptive optics systems of large format ground telescopes, yet their application to space telescopes (for a large format, segmented primary mirror with active optics) remains largely unstudied.  In this contribution present the calibration and laboratory characterization of a contactless deformable mirror prototype for a space telescope segment. The prototype is LATT, the optical surface a 1 mm thick Zerodur mirror with 19 non-contact actuators over its 40 cm diameter. The system is calibrated by adapting existing ground-based calibration techniques for the prototype. The main innovation is in the validation of these techniques in a novel environment: the system is placed in a vacuum chamber and operated in low pressure conditions, in full magnetic levitation, free of any mechanical constraints.

Items.Authors: William Schoenell, Christoph Birk, Jason Williams, Nick Konidaris, Paulo H. S. Silva
Items.Title: Control architecture for Henrietta spectrograph on the Swope Telescope
Items.Abstract: This presentation describes the development of the Henrietta instrument control software and its integration with the Swope TCS at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. Henrietta is a near-infrared, low-resolution spectrograph designed for the Swope telescope, which has recently undergone significant technological upgrades. To unify this heterogeneous environment, we employed the Chimera Observatory Control System (OCS) to create standardized interfaces for all isolated components. This high-level integration enables control algorithms, such as observation scheduling, and weather safety, to operate independently of the underlying hardware, promoting flexibility and scalability. By establishing well-defined hardware interfaces, our approach facilitates the reuse of software components across different observatories and instruments. We discuss the implementation process, challenges encountered, and the broader impact of adopting Chimera OCS for observatory automation and interoperability.

Items.Authors: Owain Snaith, Narsireddy Anugu, Dan Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Sebastien Morel, Mike Ireland, Jyotirmay Paul, Sorabh Chhabra
Items.Title: Control software framework for BIFROST, a 4-telescope J- and H-band interferometer for VLTI
Items.Abstract: BIFROST is part of the Asgard suite and is a 4-telescope interferometer in the J- and H-bands. BIFROST will be installed at the VLTI as a visitor instrument early in 2026. We will discuss the software framework for BIFROST and outline how we manage communications from different parts of Asgard, and the interaction of the various actuators and detectors during setup and observations. The final design of BIFROST will include two computers running Linux and numerous subsystems, including a group delay tracker, fibre explorer, real time display etc., which are required to conduct observations. BIFROST will interact with other parts of Asgard, and with a ESO compliant gateway computer running the VLTI observing software. Our software framework builds upon the software currently running MIRCX at CHARA and allows us to control two C-RED One near infrared cameras. The software is designed to be used via several remote GUIs, and via observing templates.

Items.Authors: Linbo Cao, Jinxin Liu, He Sun
Items.Title: Coronagraph as a spectrograph
Items.Abstract: Spectroscopic characterization is crucial for understanding stellar properties and for accurately calibrating the spectral differences between reference and target stars, which is essential for precise Point Spread Function (PSF) subtraction. However, many telescopes are not equipped with dedicated spectrographs for such characterization. In this presentation, we show a coronagraph can act as a low-resolution spectrometer: its wavelength-dependent modulation imprints spectral information onto the broadband coronagraphic PSF. We cast spectrum recovery as an inverse problem by fitting a forward PSF model to a single broadband image. Simulations and a laboratory demonstrator confirm feasibility, and we demonstrate the method on HST coronagraph data. This enables spectral inference from archival coronagraph images and relaxes color-matching constraints for PSF reference stars in future telescopes.

Items.Authors: Natalia Sanchez-Soria, James R. Fienup, Scott D. Will
Items.Title: Coronagraphic postprocessing using model-based differential imaging (MDI)
Items.Abstract: Model-based postprocessing approaches use a diffraction-based forward model to estimate the aberrated stellar PSF, which can be subtracted from a coronagraph image to reduce residual starlight. The PSF is obtained by finding model parameters that minimize the difference between the observed and predicted images. In this work, we simulated model-based differential imaging (MDI) using the coefficients of the wavefront error at the coronagraph entrance pupil as free parameters. We also explored adding measurement diversity to improve the fit of the model to the data. Our simulations assumed contrast levels and wavefront dynamics relevant to the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), using a coronagraph design and observing scenario for the EAC-1 concept design. We also simulated RDI and ADI under the same conditions. Our simulations so far show that MDI can achieve a similar performance to ADI and RDI, despite not necessarily requiring movement of the telescope.

Items.Authors: Eduardo A. Bendek, Rachel E. Morgan, Dan Sirbu, Jon Lin, Ruslan Belikov
Items.Title: Coupling free space light into the AstroPIC photonic coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requires an unprecedented contrast of 1e-10 to characterize Exo-Earth atmospheres. Conventional free-space optics struggle with the stability and wavefront error correction needed for this high-contrast imaging, jeopardizing the mission’s exoplanet yield. Integrated photonics (PICs) offer a critical solution, providing superior stability, control, and compactness to boost coronagraph performance.  However, efficiently injecting light collected from the free-space telescope into the micron-scale PIC remains a major technical hurdle that directly limits system throughput. At NASA Ames, the AstroPIC laboratory is dedicated to optimize this injection efficiency. Our research progresses from single-fiber coupling to using a microlens arrays to maximize fill factor. Future efforts include utilizing wavefront information derived from the photonic coronagraph to drive a deformable mirror for active injection optimization into the PIC

Items.Authors: Davide Sisana, Bianca Salmaso, Daniele Spiga, Stefano Basso, Akanshu Chauhan, Simone Marini, Benedetta Della Barba, Mauro Ghigo, Gabriele Vecchi, Giorgia Sironi, Giovanni Pareschi, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Claudio Ferrari, Elena Ferrari, Manuel Sanchez del Rio, Marcos Bavdaz, Ivo Ferreira
Items.Title: Critical aspects in the development of the 1.49keV channel for the BEaTriX x-ray calibration facility
Items.Abstract: BEaTriX is a compact X-ray facility at INAF-OAB (Merate, Italy), designed with two energy channels: an operational 4.51 keV beamline and a 1.49 keV beamline currently being installed. Both channels combine parabolic grazing-incidence mirrors and asymmetric Bragg crystals to produce a wide, low-divergence beam. The 1.49 keV channel uses two asymmetric Quartz (10-10) crystals for the monochromator and two asymmetric organic ADP (101) crystals for horizontal beam expansion. These crystals were characterized at INAF/Brera, IMEM-CNR, and ESRF, with a strict emphasis placed on measuring the planarity of their crystal planes, as the requirements are very tight (tens of kilometers of radius of curvature). The characterization of the ADP crystals revealed systematic errors that the instrument's capabilities were approaching their limits. After an in-depth analysis, the correction of these errors resulted in the design of an alignment tilting system for both ADP crystals.

Items.Authors: Rebeka Gy. Kiss, Zoltán Szabó, Bendegúz Koncz, L. Viktor Tóth, Gábor Battistig
Items.Title: Cryogenic characterization of InGaAsP/InP NIR LEDs
Items.Abstract: Near-infrared LEDs are employed in a growing number of space instrumentation roles; however, existing cryogenic studies address InGaAsP/InP devices only at isolated wavelengths. We characterized six InGaAsP/InP double-heterojunction LEDs with nominal emission wavelengths of 1030-1650 nm over 85-290 K, acquiring spectral and current-voltage measurements during passive warm-up. The optical and electrical temperature sensitivities are decoupled: cooling to 77 K shifts the peak emission wavelength by -42 nm at 1030 nm to -124 nm at 1650 nm, while the threshold voltage change of +0.29 to +0.36 V is independent of composition. Fixed-beta Varshni fitting (beta = 327 K) yields a composition-independent alpha = (4.7 +/- 0.2) x 10^-4 eV/K across all six devices. The threshold voltage response was linear over the full range, with no two-slope behavior as reported for AlGaInP and InGaN devices. These results support cryogenic pre-qualification of InGaAsP/InP NIR LEDs for space instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Andrea Occhiuzzi, Takumi Izawa, Kentaro Kikuno, Luca Lamagna, Tomotake Matsumura, Yutaro Sekimoto, Hayato Takakura, Giulia Barbieri Ripamonti, Elia Battistelli, Paolo de Bernardis, Fabio Columbro, Alessandro Coppolecchia, Marco De Petris, Elisabetta Marchitelli, Silvia Masi, Mahdi Najafi, Alessandro Paiella, Francesco Piacentini, Giampaolo Pisano, Simone Stellati
Items.Title: Cryogenic measurements of candidate microwave absorbers for the LiteBIRD telescope
Items.Abstract: Microwave absorber suitable for cryogenic environments are essential to mitigate stray light in the telescope of the next-generation CMB satellite LiteBIRD. To meet stringent constraints on the mass budget, residual reflectance and thermal performance at low temperatures, we investigate candidate absorbers based on STYCAST2850FT epoxy resin loaded with different activated-carbon powders and shaped into pyramidal non-reflective layer geometries. Finite-element simulations were used to optimize the low-frequency reflectance, while the dielectric and optical properties of the prototypes were experimentally characterized through broadband FTS and coherent near-field measurements in the 34−448 GHz frequency range. Cryogenic measurements were performed using dedicated setups operating down to 90 K and 2.8 K. The results reveal a strong temperature dependence of the electromagnetic properties of the investigated materials, with a significant increase in transmission observed after cooldown.

Items.Authors: Matteo Porru, Guido Cupani, Andrea Scaudo, Giorgio Calderone, Rodolfo Smiljanic, Mariagrazia Franchini, Roberto Cirami, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Paolo Cucurullo, Matteo Genoni
Items.Title: CUBES software development in Active Flexure Compensation, E2E simulator and Data Reduction Software
Items.Abstract: CUBES (Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph) is a high-efficiency spectrograph designed for the ESO VLT, targeting the near-UV wavelength range (300-405 nm) with spectral resolving powers of R>20,000 (high resolution) and R~7,000 (low resolution). CUBES recently completed its Final Design Review and entered the Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration, and Testing phase. This paper presents recent improvements in the Active Flexure Compensation (AFC) system, the End-to-End (E2E) simulator, and the Data Reduction Software (DRS).

Items.Authors: Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi, Matteo Munari, Simone D'Auria, Andrea Bianco, Giorgio Pariani, Ciro Del Vecchio, Paolo Picchi, Roland Bacon, Bernard Delabre, David Lee, Sofia Randich, Will Saunders
Items.Title: Current status of the high-resolution multiobject spectrograph (MOS-HR) for the wide-field spectroscopic telescope
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) is a planned 12-meter class dedicated spectroscopic facility for massive spectroscopic surveys. This paper presents the current status of Work Package 4.5, the High Resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph (MOS-HR) module. We describe the international team organization and optical design resulting from extensive trade-off studies, presenting its evolution driven by scientific requirements and technical constraints. Design parameters derived from science cases and astronomical community requirements are detailed. Given the critical importance of mass and volume budgets, we present envelope dimensions and mass estimates for MOS-HR. The spectrograph constructive parameters are defined, including optical fiber specifications, multiplex capability, and modular architecture. Finally, we present the structural analysis addressing mechanical stability and performance requirements for this high-resolution multi-object spectrograph.

Items.Authors: Rosly Renil, Hugo Hamman, Christopher Schollar, Martin Slabber
Items.Title: Data life cycle policies in boosting science data ops efficiency
Items.Abstract: A Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) process brings order and clarity to an observatory's data information. This structure makes it easier to achieve essential goals like keeping data secure and ensuring it’s readily accessible when needed.     This poster presents a DLM strategy used for SARAO science operations, current challenges faced and MeerKAT systems that focuses heavily on safeguarding data and enabling disaster recovery—especially important as cyber threats rise alongside the rapid expansion of digital information. By having a reliable recovery plan ready to go, observatories can reduce the financial damage and reputational harm caused by unexpected events.

Items.Authors: Shinji Fujita, Kenichi Karatsu, Shiro Ikeda, Akio Taniguchi, Akira Endo, Tatsuya Takekoshi, Yuri Nishimura, Kotaro Kohno, Stefanie Brackenhoff, Arend Moerman, Juri Yamanaka, Yoichi Tamura
Items.Title: Data processing and calibration pipeline for DESHIMA 2.0 observations on the ASTE telescope
Items.Abstract: Microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKIDs) enable multiplexed spectroscopy at submillimeter wavelengths. DESHIMA 2.0, an on-chip filterbank spectrometer on the 10-m ASTE telescope in Chile, is among the first instruments to demonstrate wideband MKID spectroscopy on sky. While it provides simultaneous spectra over a broad band, the data require careful processing.  The responsivity and noise of individual KIDs vary between days due to atmospheric and instrumental conditions. Detector flagging, performance tracking, and calibration are essential. Atmospheric correction, responsivity normalization, and frequency alignment are required to convert raw timestreams into usable spectra or maps.  In this poster, we present the DESHIMA 2.0 data-processing workflow, including detector checks, automated masking, and calibration. We show how these procedures improve the fidelity and reproducibility of the final data and discuss implications for future DESHIMA and TIFUUN observations.

Items.Authors: Alexander Lapuente, P. S. Barry, C. S. Benson, C. M. Bradford, T. L. R. Brien, S. Doyle, V. Gómez-Rivera, S. Hailey-Dunsheath, J. Hernández-Aguilar, J. L. Hérnandez-Rebollar, D. H. Hughes, E. Kane, K. S. Karkare, R. McGeehan, R. Naranjo-Romero, A. Papageorgiou, J. G. Redford, I. Rodríguez-Montoya, S. Rowe, D. O. Sánchez-Arguelles, S. Savorgnano, A. Tan, M. Becerril-Tapia, J. Vega-Méndez
Items.Title: Data reduction pipeline for the SuMAC millimeter-wave spectrometer at the LMT
Items.Abstract: We present the data reduction and analysis pipeline for the SuperSpec-MUSCAT Collaboration (SuMaC) along with several key science data products. In Summer 2025, SuperSpec on-chip spectrometers operating from 190-300 GHz at R~200 were deployed on the MUSCAT focal plane at the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), obtaining several days of high-quality on-sky data. Analysis of these data has been used to characterize noise performance and study spectra of various astrophysical sources, establishing the instrument’s viability for future line intensity mapping (LIM) deployments. We discuss calibration methods, data processing options, and preliminary analysis of the observed sources.
